summary:
RogSi pairs the free red legendary Rograkh (fuel for Mox Amber, Drum, Mantle, Culling, Plunge and Flare, and a commander for free spells) with Silas Renn's artifact recursion. It's a cEDH Breach + Oracle shell. All 7 Spellbook lines and all 14 attestation items are re-verified against the canonical list.

Rules surprises: Samut's split second locks you out too, though triggers still happen; Demonic Counsel finds nothing before delirium, since there are no Demons; Mnemonic Betrayal can't play lands. One flag: your own Vexing Bauble counters your free spells and {0} escapes unless Hexing Squelcher is out.

interactions.title: Partners: U/B/R identity, separate commander tax, a free red legendary body
interactions.ruling: Rograkh (mana cost {0}, red) and Silas Renn (blue-black) are both partners. Together they give U/B/R color identity. Each commander's tax is tracked separately, so Rograkh stays free on his first cast and costs {2} after that. Effects that check whether you control a commander are happy with either one, which covers Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat and both modes of Jeska's Will.
interactions.short: Separate taxes; first Rograkh cast is free; either partner turns on commander-presence free spells.

oracle.quote: If you control a commander, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost.

rulings.quote: Once the game begins, your two commanders are tracked separately. If you cast one, you won't have to pay an additional {2} the first time you cast the other. A player loses the game after having been dealt 21 damage from any one of them, not from both of them combined.
An effect that checks whether you control your commander is satisfied if you control one or both of your two commanders.

interactions.title: Rograkh as a resource: Mox Amber, Springleaf Drum, Paradise Mantle, Culling the Weak, Infernal Plunge, Flare of Duplication
interactions.ruling:
A free legendary red creature fuels several cards:
- **Mox Amber:** taps for red, and blue or black once Silas is out too.
- **Springleaf Drum:** taps him for mana.
- **Paradise Mantle:** makes him tap for any color, though only once he no longer has summoning sickness.
- **Sacrifice outlets:** Culling the Weak ({B}{B}{B}{B}), Infernal Plunge ({R}{R}{R}) and Diabolic Intent all sacrifice him as an additional cost.
- **Flare of Duplication:** a free copy spell if you sacrifice him, since he's a nontoken red creature.

After he's sacrificed he can go to the command zone and come back for {2}.

oracle.quote: You may sacrifice a nontoken red creature rather than pay this spell's mana cost.
{T}: Add one mana of any color among legendary creatures and planeswalkers you control.

rulings.quote: Players can only respond once this spell has been cast and all its costs have been paid. No one can try to destroy the creature you sacrificed to prevent you from casting this spell.

interactions.title: Silas Renn: cast one artifact card from your graveyard this turn, at normal timing
interactions.ruling: When Silas deals combat damage to a player, his trigger targets an artifact card in your graveyard, and you may cast it that turn. That holds even if Silas has left the battlefield. You pay its costs, and alternative costs are allowed. The trigger doesn't change timing, so a non-flash artifact still needs your main phase with an empty stack. Once cast, the card is a new object, so you can't cast it twice. It doesn't work on lands.

oracle.quote: Whenever Silas Renn deals combat damage to a player, choose target artifact card in your graveyard. You may cast that card this turn.

rulings.quote: Silas Renn doesn't change when you can cast the target artifact card. For example, if you target an artifact card without flash, you can cast it only during your main phase when the stack is empty.
Casting the card causes it to leave your graveyard and become a new object. You can't cast it multiple times.
You may cast that card this turn even if Silas Renn leaves the battlefield.

interactions.title: Vexing Bauble counters your own free spells (Rograkh, Moxen, LED, Fierce Guardianship, Flare, Breach escapes for {0})
interactions.short: Own Bauble hits own free spells; Squelcher or a pre-combo sac solves it.

flag.note: Vexing Bauble counters the deck's own free spells and {0} escapes (Rograkh, Moxen, LED, Petal, Fierce Guardianship, Flare, Breach + Grinding Station). Have Hexing Squelcher out, or sacrifice Bauble first.

oracle.quote: Whenever a player casts a spell, if no mana was spent to cast it, counter that spell.
Spells you control can't be countered.

rulings.quote: If a spell is cast with an alternative cost that includes mana (such as flashback), Vexing Bauble's first ability won't trigger and won't counter that spell. Similarly, if a spell is cast without paying its mana cost, but the player did pay mana for additional costs such as from kicker or from Thorn of Amethyst, Vexing Bauble's first ability won't trigger and won't counter that spell.

A spell or ability that counters spells can still target any spell that can't be countered. When that spell or ability resolves, the spell that can't be countered won't be countered, but any additional effects of the countering spell or ability will still happen.

interactions.title: Samut gives your instants and sorceries split second, but triggers still happen
interactions.ruling: While one of your Samut-boosted spells is on the stack, no one can cast spells or activate non-mana abilities. That includes you: you can't Flare, Swat or Guardianship on top of your own split-second spell. Mana abilities like LED and Lotus Petal still work. Triggers still happen: storm copies Brain Freeze, and Vexing Bauble still counters a free split-second spell. Once the split-second spell leaves the stack, everyone can act again.

oracle.quote: Instant and sorcery spells you control have split second. (As long as a spell with split second is on the stack, players can't cast spells or activate abilities that aren't mana abilities.)

rulings.quote: Split second doesn't stop triggered abilities from triggering. If one does, its controller puts it on the stack and chooses targets for it, if any. Those abilities will resolve as normal.
If the resolution of a triggered ability involves casting a spell, that spell can't be cast if a spell with split second is on the stack.

interactions.title: Thassa's Oracle + Consultation / Tainted Pact; Breach lines (LED + Brain Freeze, LED + Wheel, Wheel + Jeska's Will, Petal + Brain Freeze, Grinding Station + Mox Amber)
interactions.ruling:
**Oracle wins:** exile your library with Consultation or Tainted Pact (100 distinct names), then Oracle's ETB wins.

**Breach loops:** LED escapes for {0} to fuel repeated Brain Freezes or Wheels. Jeska's Will counts the hand of an opponent who has just wheeled. The Grinding Station + Mox Amber loop mills three per cycle, and Amber taps for red from Rograkh.

All seven Spellbook lines are present. Vexing Bauble stops the {0} escapes (see rogsi-04).

Cast Lion's Eye Diamond from your graveyard for its escape cost by exiling three cards besides Brain Freeze from your graveyard.
Cast the artifact from your graveyard for its escape cost by paying {0} and exiling three cards from your graveyard.

interactions.title: Final Fortune / Warrior's Oath: the lose trigger is real here
interactions.ruling: Both give an extra turn with a delayed "you lose the game" trigger at that turn's end step. This list has no Obeka or Sundial, so the extra turn must win or the trigger has to be answered some other way. If the extra turn is skipped, you don't lose.

oracle.quote: Take an extra turn after this one. At the beginning of that turn's end step, you lose the game.

rulings.quote: If you end up skipping the extra turn that is gained, you do not lose the game.

interactions.title: Demonic Counsel needs delirium; Mnemonic Betrayal casts but never plays lands; Undercity Sewers is fetchable
interactions.ruling:
**Demonic Counsel:** without delirium it finds only a Demon, and the canonical list has none. With four or more card types in your graveyard, it finds any card.

**Mnemonic Betrayal:** lets you cast spells from opponents' exiled graveyards this turn, with any mana, at normal timing. You can't play their lands. Cards you don't cast go back at the next end step, and a permanent you cast stays.

**Undercity Sewers:** an Island Swamp, so your fetchlands can find it.

oracle.quote: Delirium — If there are four or more card types among cards in your graveyard, instead search your library for any card, put it into your hand, then shuffle.

rulings.quote: You can’t play land cards exiled this way.
Only the cards that remain in exile are returned to their owners’ graveyards. For example, a permanent spell cast this way will remain on the battlefield.
